title: tc-retrieval-inspector
description:
The chunks retrieved for an answer – score, source and place, freshness, whether the answer used them – and the
misses the app reports.

query.description: The query the chunks were retrieved for

chunks.description: The chunks, in rank order – the first is the best match

misses.description: Chunks the app reports should have been retrieved and weren't

cutoff.description: The score below which chunks are left out of the prompt – marked on every score bar; unset marks none

maxScore.description: The top of the score scale – defaults to 1, or the highest score when that is higher

show.description: Which chunks show: "all", "used" (by the answer) or "unused"

selected.description: The id of the open chunk, or null

profile.description: How fast sources go stale, for chunks without their own `profile` – see tc-validity-badge

now.description: The moment freshness is counted to, in epoch ms – defaults to when each badge connected

openHandled.description: Open source fires tc-open-source and the link doesn't navigate on its own; chunks without a url get the button

maxHeight.description: The list's height before it scrolls, in px

text.description: The chunk's text, as it was given to the model

score.description: The retrieval score – higher is closer

location.description: Where in the source, in words: "p. 12 · §3.2"

position.description: Its place among the document's chunks: { index: 3, count: 37 } is the fourth of 37 (index from 0)

url.description: Opens the source; with `open-handled` the app opens it instead

observed.description: When the source was published or last updated – sets the freshness band

profile.description: How fast this source goes stale – defaults to the inspector's `profile`

citation.description: The marker the answer cites it with – "2" shows as [2]

ValidityTime.description: A moment: epoch ms, an ISO date string or a Date

ValidityProfileName.description: Built-in decay profiles – fast: hours and days (prices, status, news) · standard: weeks and months · slow: years (reference material) · lasting: never decays

ValidityProfile.description: The band boundaries, as an age in days: younger than `high` is high, than `good` good, than `aging` aging; older is stale

text.description: The passage that was missed, or the start of it

reason.description: Why it counts as a miss, in a line

score.description: Its score, if the app scored it – often just under the cutoff

RetrievalMiss.description: A chunk the app says should have been retrieved and wasn't – from eval labels, a reviewer, or a later check
